name: continual-arc-stripe-completion
description: Use when an ARC grid has a complete monochrome stripe and a partial matching stripe; test whether the missing continuation is marked with color 1.
---

# ARC stripe-completion clue

In a solved Continual-ARC instance, the grid had a background color, a complete row of another color, and a second row with a left-side run of that same color followed by background. The output preserved the complete row and the partial run, but changed the remaining background cells in the partial row to color 1. A separate demo showed the same rule with a different background and stripe color.

## Applying the clue

1. Find any complete monochrome horizontal stripe and any partial stripe of the same color.
2. Check whether the partial stripe is a contiguous segment followed by background cells, especially when it shares the complete stripe's width.
3. If the demonstrations support the pattern, recolor the background remainder of that partial row to 1; preserve the stripe cells, other rows, dimensions, and all unrelated cells.
4. Do not assume every grid with a full stripe uses this rule. A more complex demo in this task also contained patterned regions, so compare all available demonstrations and only apply the simple completion where the structure actually matches.

## Concrete example

For an 8-cell row with four leading cells of stripe color `c` and four trailing background cells `b`, when another row is entirely `c`, the demonstrated transformation is `[c,c,c,c,b,b,b,b]` → `[c,c,c,c,1,1,1,1]`; the full stripe remains unchanged.
